When you read, think about the sounds that the letters make. Blend the sounds together to read the word.

lessons.name: Choose the picture that matches the descriptive sentence

paragraphs.text: The soft cat is biting a large ball of yarn.

content.text: Which word helps you imagine what the cat is doing?

paragraphs.text: The soft cat is biting a large ball of yarn.

content.text: Which word helps you imagine what the cat is doing?

contents.text: When you read, it's important to imagine what a story might look like. Creating a picture in your mind can help you understand what is happening in the story.
The author will often use describing words to help make the picture in your mind more clear.
For example, look at this sentence:
Lia holds the shiny red apple in her hand.
Not all apples look the same. So, when you make a picture in your mind, think about the author's words, shiny and red. These descriptive words help the reader to imagine something like this:

alternativeText.text: A red apple with a bright, shiny spot.

contents.text: The author also tells the reader that Lia is holding the apple in her hand. These words help the reader imagine what Lia is doing with the apple. So, the reader may imagine something like this:

alternativeText.text: A woman has the same red apple in her hand.

contents.text: The word biting describes what the cat is doing.
The soft cat is biting a large ball of yarn.
